headline: UCL commits to racial equality action in the context of coronavirus
detail: An institutional plan for 2020-21 covering fair admissions after exam disruption, the BAME degree awarding gap, belonging, and hardship including digital poverty.
quote: UCL’s Equality, Diversity and Inclusion team are currently working at speed on an institutional plan for 2020-21 and it will include specific action on racial equality in the context of coronavirus.
notes: Published four days after the killing of George Floyd. The newsletter connects it to the pandemic through the disproportionate mortality figures cited in the same issue.

headline: UCL cites ONS finding that Covid deaths are four times likelier among black adults
detail: Used to argue that the disparity could not be explained by health inequalities alone.
quote: According to the ONS, Covid-19 deaths are four times more likely among black adults than those of white ethnicity in the UK.
notes: UCL relaying an ONS finding. The ONS publication is a stage 2 retrieval target; the figure must not be repeated as established until the primary source is checked.

headline: Student Centre entry conditional on temperature check, booking and face covering
detail: Bookable Monday to Friday, 100 people a day maximum, ID and confirmation required at reception.
quote: You will be asked to take your temperature at the entrance of the Student Centre.
notes: The daily cap tightened from the 130 announced on 26 May to 100 in practice.

headline: Oxford vaccine phase III trial to vaccinate 500 UCLH staff volunteers
detail: UCL's Vax-Hub collaboration with the Jenner Institute supplied the manufacturing platform the Oxford team adapted.
quote: Screening for the ‘phase III’ trial of the vaccine began at the end of May, and researchers plan to begin vaccinations in 500 healthy UCLH staff volunteers in June.
notes: Six months before the national rollout began. UCL's involvement in the vaccine is upstream of the vaccination programme, not part of receiving it.

headline: UCL works with Camden Council to make commuting possible without public transport
detail: Aimed at making cycling viable for staff returning under the pilots.
quote: we’re working with Camden Council and other local organisations to make it easier to commute to UCL without using public transport
notes: Transport is named repeatedly as the constraint on returning to campus, and here as a reason for a borough-level partnership.

headline: UCL sets policy for staff caught by the new quarantine on UK arrivals
detail: Staff abroad were told to return two weeks before they were needed and to work from home, volunteer through UCL Together, stay on furlough or take paid leave.
quote: Staff currently living abroad or wishing to travel abroad should be aware that the Government has introduced a two-week self-isolation period for anyone entering the UK on or after 8 June
notes: Filed on 8 June, the date the national rule took effect; UCL's guidance was published on 4 June, four days ahead of it. A negative lag.

headline: Face-covering guidance issued distinguishing coverings from PPE
detail: Coverings required when moving around, removable at a desk two metres from others, with PPE reserved for those who need it and exemptions acknowledged.
quote: Importantly, a face covering is a precautionary measure and not the same as personal protective equipment (PPE), which includes surgical masks and tight-fitting face masks. PPE must continue to be reserved only for those who need it.
notes: Exemptions are named explicitly for respiratory conditions and for deaf staff and those with hearing loss who rely on lip reading.

headline: Gold, Silver and Bronze structure replaced by a Crisis Leadership Team
detail: The command structure adopted in April gave way to an implementation framework once the closure and planning work was done.
quote: We now need to focus on implementing plans and have moved away from the GSB structure towards a new framework. The focus of the new framework, starting from 8 June, continues to be set by the Provost and is supported by a Crisis Leadership Team.
notes: Filed on the effective date of 8 June; announced 5 June. The second reorganisation of UCL's decision-making in three months.

headline: All library loans extended to 1 October with no late penalties
detail: Correcting a technical fault that had brought some due dates forward.
quote: All library loans are now due on 1 October or for some students, at the end of their programme of study.
notes: Extends the 5 June date set on 18 March.

headline: Provost asks for review of buildings named after eugenicists
detail: Following the recommendations of the Inquiry into the History of Eugenics at UCL, chaired by Professor Iyiola Solanke, with a recommendation due to Council on 18 June.
quote: UCL’s President & Provost Professor Michael Arthur has today formally asked the university’s ‘Buildings Naming and Renaming Committee’ immediately to start the process of reviewing the current naming of spaces and buildings after two prominent eugenicists Francis Galton and Karl Pearson.
notes: Not part of UCL's pandemic response, and included only because the pandemic newsletters were the channel that carried it. Filter on category governance if the timeline is read as a pandemic record.

headline: UCL denames the Galton and Pearson spaces
detail: Decided by the Provost and ratified by Council, with signs removed immediately.
quote: UCL has today announced it will dename spaces and buildings named after two prominent eugenicists Francis Galton and Karl Pearson.
notes: Eight days from the Provost's request to the decision. As above, contemporaneous with the pandemic rather than part of the response to it.

headline: Reopening widens from nine areas to about forty
detail: With line managers contacting staff individually and no compulsion to return.
quote: We are now in the third week of pilot schemes, with nine areas of UCL reopened. From today, we’re planning to restart activity in some 40 more areas of the university.
notes: The step from pilot to programme. Three months after the closure of 20 March.

headline: Over 180 live UCL projects investigating coronavirus, almost half externally funded
quote: There are now over 180 live projects across all UCL’s faculties investigating coronavirus and its impact. Of these, almost half are externally funded.
notes: Up from the hundred reported on 15 May.

headline: Face-to-face invigilated exams ruled unlikely for 2020-21
detail: Replaced by short, timed, online and un-invigilated exams, with staff required to confirm assessment modes by 24 July for the August Module Catalogue update.
quote: It is highly likely that we will be unable to deliver face-to-face invigilated exams next year, and students need clarity about how they will be assessed.
notes: Consumer legislation is given as the reason for the July deadline, which is a legal rather than epidemiological constraint on the timing.

headline: Emergency Timetabling Policy approved by the Crisis Management Team
detail: With a revised timetabling process for 2020-21 and FAQs on how the Temporary Operating Model would work in practice.
quote: An Emergency Timetabling Policy has been approved by the Crisis Management Team and our Timetabling FAQs provide some further granularity about how the Temporary Operating Model will operate in practice.
notes: The mechanism by which the Temporary Operating Model reached individual rooms and hours, which is what determined how many people were on campus in autumn 2020.

headline: All staff and postgraduate researchers asked to complete a workstation assessment
detail: A display screen equipment assessment for the home working environment, with issues referred to line managers.
quote: To ensure you can work comfortably, UCL is asking all staff and postgraduate researchers to complete an online workstation assessment.
notes: Three months into remote working, which is when the temporary arrangement started being treated as a workplace.

headline: REF2021 submission deadline reset to 31 March 2021
detail: With the impact assessment period extended to 31 December 2020 and the exercise resuming on 31 July 2020. The staff census date of 31 July 2020 was unchanged.
quote: The revised REF submission deadline is now noon on 31 March 2021 for all elements of submissions. They have also confirmed an extended assessment period for impact to 31 December 2020.
notes: Resolves the indefinite postponement announced on 25 March. A sector-level decision by the funding bodies; the primary announcement belongs on the sector track in stage 2.

headline: Library Click and Collect opens at the Portico entrance
detail: Up to ten books per request, collected 12.00 to 15.00 Monday to Friday, with ID, confirmation email and a face covering required on campus.
quote: Requesting will be made available on Explore on Friday 19 June and fetching will begin next Monday, 22 June.
notes: Filed on 22 June, the date collection began. The first library service of any kind since the closure of 20 March, and it is contactless.
